Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 3-day history of acute diarrhea, vomiting, subjective fever, and peri-umbilical pain; likely infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk; plan for urgent clinic assessment and stool testing; continue oral rehydration in small sips and bland diet; ED precautions given.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe diarrhea and vomiting for 3 days with subjective high temperature and central abdominal pain.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset: 3 days ago.
  - Course: Started as very watery stools; now very loose. Ongoing vomiting; unable to keep liquids down. No improvement despite ORS use.
  - Today: At least 4 bowel movements; lost count overall.
  - Last emesis: ~2 hours before consult after attempting breakfast.
  - Urination: Passing urine; last void ~1 hour before consult; urine color not observed.
- Character/associations:
  - Diarrhea: Very loose; initially watery; ≥4 times today; no blood.
  - Vomiting: With liquids and solids; “throwing up everything.”
  - Abdominal pain: Peri-umbilical, very sore to touch, comes and goes; episodes associated with urge to defecate.
  - Fever: Feels “boiling/roasting”; no measured temperature (no thermometer).
  - No rash.
- Exposures:
  - Close contact: Brother with similar symptoms; reports many at his school ill. No recent travel abroad.
- Baseline bowel habits: Normally 1 formed bowel movement each morning; no prior diarrhea or constipation.
- Gynecologic: LMP ~2 weeks ago. Not on contraception. Not having regular sexual intercourse.
- Medications tried for this illness: Oral rehydration solution (salt-sugar mix) ~3 times/day for past 2 days; vomiting has limited tolerance.
- Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No blood in stool or urine; no rash.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions documented.
- Dysmenorrhea: Uses ibuprofen as needed.
- No prior abdominal problems or surgeries reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.
- Living situation: Lives with brother and mother.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Occasional (“a pint from time to time”).
- Illicit drugs: Denies.

Family History:
- Brother currently has similar gastrointestinal symptoms. No other family history mentioned.

Physical Examination:

Investigations:
- Planned: Stool sample to evaluate for bacterial infection; in-clinic assessment of hydration status.
- No test results available at time of consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial etiology not excluded)
  - Assessment: Acute onset diarrhea, vomiting, fever, abdominal cramping; household contact with similar illness; no blood in stool.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain stool sample urgently at clinic to rule out bacterial infection.
    - Supportive care: Continue oral rehydration solution using very small, frequent sips to improve tolerance.
    - Diet: Simple/bland foods (e.g., toast, biscuits) as tolerated; avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk per advice.
- Issue 2: Risk of dehydration
  - Assessment: Ongoing vomiting limiting oral intake; still urinating (last 1 hour ago), which is reassuring but at risk if intake remains poor.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent in-person appointment for hydration assessment.
    - Strict return/ED precautions: If worsening, unable to keep fluids down, signs of dehydration, or feeling more unwell, attend Emergency Department; call clinic if symptoms escalate.
- Issue 3: Symptom management and follow-up
  - Plan:
    - Continue ORS with tiny, frequent sips.
    - Book urgent clinic visit via support line to expedite stool testing and hydration check.
    - Monitor urine frequency and any presence of blood in stool/urine; report changes.

Medications (as documented):
- Vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not fully documented beyond daily use).
- Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Oral rehydration solution (salt-sugar mix) ~3 times/day for 2 days.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergy status not documented; vitals not recorded; medication doses/routes/frequencies largely unspecified; pregnancy status not explicitly addressed (LMP 2 weeks ago, not sexually active regularly); immunization and problem list not reviewed.
● Internal conflicts: None significant; patient reports inability to keep fluids but is still passing urine (last 1 hour prior), suggesting not yet severely dehydrated.
● Transcript quality: Occasional pauses/inaudible or incomplete responses; overall history and plan understandable.
